title: SGL3D fog: bound a point or spot light's inverse square by the froxel's size
abstract:
Closes #262.

A point light near the camera left soft, discrete puffs in the volumetric fog: Hyperdrive's cyan engine light, 2.9 m behind the craft. Fog injection lights each froxel at one jittered sample, cycling through 16 positions. With `1/max(d², 1e-4)`, a sample landing centimetres from the light took thousands of times the froxel's light. The 0.9 reprojected history then held each spike in world space, so a still light pulsed with the jitter and a moving one left puffs behind.

## References (RD-2)
| Source | What it does |
|---|---|
| Godot b130438 `volumetric_fog_process.glsl` | Omni and spot lights take `get_omni_attenuation`, floored only at `max(dist, 0.0001)`, with a default decay of 1 (1/d). Only its area lights clamp `d ≥ 1` m "against extreme flickering". |
| Bevy 9d12036 `volumetric_fog.wesl` | `getDistanceAttenuation` with the same 1e-4 floor; per-pixel IGN jitter, no history. |
| Hillaire 2015, Frostbite (slides 17, 22, 25) | One Halton-jittered sample per froxel with a 5% blend. Lists "Moving lights leave trails. Use neighbour clamping?" as open. |
| Unreal, practice only, no code | `r.VolumetricFog.InverseSquaredLightDistanceBiasScale`: "Scales the amount added to the inverse squared falloff denominator. This effectively removes the spike from inverse squared falloff that causes extreme aliasing." The bias is the volume cell's size. |
| Unity VolumetricLighting sample b5b0713 (MIT, allowed) | Bounded point-light falloff in the fog: `1/(1 + 25 d²/range²)`. |

The shared treatment is a bounded near field. This PR takes Unreal's form, since it scales with the froxel.

## Change
- In the fog's point and spot evaluation only, the inverse square takes in its denominator the squared diagonal of the froxel's view-space bounding box: its slice's depth and, on each axis across the frame, the extent of its corners at both ends. It is the same size wherever the froxel lies on screen.
- `light_reach.wgsl` stays the formula's single owner. It takes the bias as a parameter; every surface caller passes 0, so surface shading is unchanged.
- Rectangles are unchanged: their light in the fog is already bounded by solid angle.
- Trade-off: within about a froxel's diagonal of a light, its fog falls short of the inverse square, and more so where `Fog::length` makes slices deep. This is recorded in the fog provenance header, the README and the CHANGELOG.

## Tests
- `a_still_point_light_holds_its_froxel_steady_over_the_jitter_cycle`: a still point light at the centre of a 0.6 m-deep near froxel must hold that froxel within 25% over a 16-frame jitter cycle. The bound comes from the bias, not a measurement: every sample lies within half the diagonal b, so `1/(d²+b²)` stays within `[1/(1.25 b²), 1/b²]`. On main it ranged 6.03–12.47 (2.07×).
- The still-light test runs at the screen centre and at the top-left and bottom-right corners, with the light at the centre of each froxel's view-space box.
- `a_light_holds_the_same_fog_on_either_side_of_the_screen`: a light near a froxel's centre and its mirror image across the view's axis must hold the same fog. This covers the frame's corners and a mid-screen cell. The review's oblique corner-pair measure fails it: 0.0538 against 0.0442 at the top-left corner and its mirror.
- `froxels_far_smaller_than_their_distance_to_a_light_keep_its_falloff`: froxels a few centimetres across, 4 m or more from a light, keep its physical falloff within half-float rounding.
- Mutations, each reverted by restoring a saved copy:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| No bias | Still-light test fails: 6.03–12.47, the same as main |
| 0.01 × the bias | Still-light test fails: 2.36–3.10 |
| 1000 × the bias | Far-light test fails, 5% dimmer; the still-light test fails as unlit |
| One oblique corner pair, the previous measure | Mirror test fails |

Not caught: a depth-only bias. It is symmetric, and the history damps its jitter swing inside the 1.25 bound.

- The existing fog tests, including the single-scattering integral, still pass.

## Evidence
Measured through Hyperdrive's capture harness, with SGL patched to base 94ab896 against this branch, at the owner's Ultra settings, on an Apple M5 with Metal.

**Fog GPU time (RD-6).** 1920×1080 on Meridian's tunnel route, 100 measured frames per run, three runs each, interleaved base/fix:

| Pass | Base, median ms | Fix, median ms |
|---|---|---|
| Fog injection | 1.765 / 1.782 / 1.745 (mean 1.764) | 1.677 / 1.835 / 1.840 (mean 1.784) |
| Fog filter | 0.098–0.101 | 0.098–0.102 |
| Fog integration | 0.043 | 0.043 |

The injection's p95 is 2.31–2.43 ms on base and 2.42–2.46 ms with the fix. The +1% median is within run-to-run noise.

**Puffs.** Hyperdrive's cyan engine light (intensity 8, range 9 m, 3.9 m from the camera) in the tunnel at 60 Hz, frames 118–135. This is the light's fog contribution: fog on minus that light's `fog_energy` 0.

| | Base | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Brightest 16 px block | 0.008–0.088 (puffs) | 0.001–0.002 |
| Mean frame-to-frame change | 0.017 | 0.000 |

**Sawtooth.** A still craft, idle engine light, rear panel:

| | Base | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Largest frame-to-frame rise | 0.00124, a 16-frame sawtooth | 0.00015, steady |

**Trade-off, measured.** Hyperdrive's fog is 1200 m long, so its near slices are about 2.4 m deep. That bias is large, and this light's halo all but disappears. Hyperdrive has since set the engine light's `fog_energy` to 0 (hyperdrive#173). With Godot's default 64 m fog, a point light 1–2 m from fog 10 m out loses about 14–39% of its near-field fog.

Captures, local in Mission Control's `.mc/captures/puffs/262/`:
- `moving-engine-fog-contribution-{base,fix}-f118-135.png`
- `moving-game-frames-base-vs-fix-f123-125.png`
- `stationary-sawtooth-base-vs-fix.png`

The owner judges the look.

## Validation
`bun scripts/tasks.ts check` passes on the branch merged with main 91a3810: sgl-3d's 381 native tests, WASM and the browser lanes.
